before.version_domain_note: Rolls back the excel_html second-authority artifact and rewrites derived HTML with no database write and no version field; independent of working_paper history.

after.version_domain_note: BLOCKED for Task 19, not migrated. This endpoint rolls back storage/projects/{pid}/excel_html/{file_stem}.structure.json and rewrites the derived HTML. It cannot enter the unified protocol as written, for two reasons that are facts about its signature rather than judgements: (1) it has no wp_id at all -- it is keyed by file_stem, so there is no workpaper scope to open a content version against, and no content_revision to advance; (2) its route uses the numeric version as a resource key (POST /versions/{file_stem}/rollback/{version}), which Requirement 10.6 forbids outright. The whole excel_html module is a live parallel authority (its own structure.json, its own version snapshots, its own edit lock, its own xlsx writeback) reachable through router_registry. Resolving it means either binding the store to workpaper identity or deleting the sidecar under Requirement 12.9 -- a product decision with no equivalence evidence yet, which Requirement 12.7's 'equivalent evidence and a rollback point before deletion' explicitly gates. Recorded here so Task 20's gate sees a reason rather than an unexplained red row.

The lane follows a manifest fact rather than a preference: workpaper_sync_entry_manifest.json pins the F2 entry (xlsx/gt-f2-stocktake-bundle) at capability=single_onlyoffice, so the OOXML body is the authority (Requirement 2.11) and the projection lane refuses it by construction. before.version_domain_note: Restores working_paper.parsed_data from wp_migration_snapshots through raw SQL and only flushes; no version increment, so a rollback is invisible to every version consumer and to the editor base.

after.version_domain_note: Task 19: the template-migration rollback now writes working_paper.parsed_data and advances the single business content_revision inside one transaction whose only commit outlet is ContentMutationService.commit_html_projection(...). It picks the projection lane because the content it restores IS the structured projection -- there are no OOXML bytes to publish as a representation, and fabricating a blank xlsx is what Requirement 3.9 forbids. capability=single_html is declared at the call site, so the plan-level refusal stays reachable; a workpaper that really has a published OO representation is refused by the database-fact check instead of silently forking its JSON projection behind the authoritative OOXML (Requirement 2.11). It writes no version field and owns no commit. Remaining debt is delegated, not local: the sibling migrate_workpaper() still writes parsed_data on its own and is unadjudicated -- template migration is not one of this task's six domains.

before.version_domain_note: Copies the current artifact into a .versions snapshot and increments working_paper.file_version itself; the snapshot name is derived from the pre-increment version, so snapshot naming and the version counter are coupled to increment order.

after.version_domain_note: Task 19: this method is no longer a version owner and no longer a content writer. It copies the CURRENT artifact into a .versions snapshot -- not one byte of content changes -- yet it used to run working_paper.file_version += 1, which both invented a version indistinguishable from its predecessor and made a fourth writer contend for the same counter as WOPI PutFile, the offline upload and the structure save. The snapshot name now follows the counter that actually moves (content_revision, advanced only by the ContentMutationService CAS) and this method only reads it. The return payload reports content_revision / snapshot_of_revision instead of a new_version it invented; there is no frontend caller of POST /save-version, and the only backend consumer returns the dict verbatim.
